newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Postbank listing not until 1998.
newsitem.headline: German Postbank listing not until 1998.

text.p: Deutsche Postbank AG, the banking arm of the former Deutsche Bundespost, confirmed on Wednesday that there was not enough time left to list its shares on the stock market this year.
"For reasons of time this is no longer possible," a company spokesman said.

German government coalition sources recently said it was probably no longer possible to list the company's shares on stock exchanges this year, and that the government was thinking of "parking" the shares with development agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW).
A finance ministry spokeswoman would not comment on specific plans, saying only "We are studying all our options."

Such an interim solution would allow the government to gain revenue this year from a stock sale that would take place next year at the earliest. This could help Bonn in its bid to qualify for European monetary union.
But Postbank appears to disagree with selling the shares first to KfW and then to the market.
The Postbank spokesman said the company preferred "a pure stock listing".
